Folks,

Quick heads-up: Medisys sent back the order form with a couple of redlines that raise export-control and controller/processor role questions. I pulled the redlines into the attached Export_Control_Matrix and a draft OrderForm PDF that highlights the lines.

Top asks I want us to coordinate on before we reply:
- Identify where we need a narrow "export-control" flag in the order form (they've added host-country export language).
- Confirm which SCCs variant we should attach and who we list as controller vs processor in the DPA (they'd like Redwood to accept controller status for a subset of processing).
- Decide whether we require a Private deployment or KMS carveout for EU-regulated buckets — procurement is asking for an answer by EOD Wednesday.

Please review the matrix and the redline PDF (attached). Ben/Olga — can you triage the DPA redline and propose one short paragraph for the order form that flags export-controlled material and indicates routing/escalation? Laura/Neha — can you confirm internal ops implications for a private deployment/KMS ask so we can provide realistic timelines/costs?

Thanks,
Jonas

Jonas —

Thanks, skimmed the matrix. A couple of quick notes from legal/contract side:
- SCCs: recommend we attach the standard EU SCCs (2021 modules) and an exhibit that maps each data category to controller/processor responsibilities. That keeps us conservative but clear.
- Controller ask: we should push back on taking controller obligations for customer data unless it's clearly data we host and configure on their behalf. We can offer a limited "processing-by-contract" statement for logs/ops metadata but not primary patient records.
- Export control: add a short clause in the order form that says any export-controlled data requires explicit written acceptance and routing to our Private offering or approved KMS configuration. Keep the language non-blocking but conditional.

I'll draft the two paragraphs (order form + DPA exhibit) and upload as a suggested redline by EOD. Olga — if you have preferred language for SCCs mapping, I can slot it into the PDF.

-Ben

Ben Carter

Adding legal redlines inline — draft attached. Key points I pushed:
1) SCCs exhibit: include a short mapping table (we can reuse the template in the Drive link) and a fallback statement that we will apply the latest EU SCCs with standard liability caps.
2) Export-control paragraph (order form): proposed language below —

"Export-Controlled Data: Customer represents and warrants that any data designated as subject to export control or similar laws will be clearly identified in the Order Form. Processing of Export-Controlled Data requires a separate written agreement and may require dedicated hosting, additional compliance controls, and/or a managed KMS. Redwood will notify Customer of any additional costs or lead times required to support such data."

3) Roles: proposed DPA wording clarifies that Customer is Controller and Redwood is Processor except for telemetry/aggregated metrics (we accept processor role only; cannot be Controller for customer-submitted PHI). If they insist on controller obligations, we can propose a limited addendum that defines joint-control narrowly for a specific data subset — but that requires Privates + KMS.

I've attached a redline (OrderForm_MediSys_20251101_redline.pdf) and a DPA clause doc. Ben — take the SCCs exhibit wording and produce the final redline for signature. Laura/Neha — see "ops impact" below:
- Private deployment: minimum lead time 6 weeks for node provisioning + security review; initial cost estimate attached as a short note.
- KMS integration (customer key): depends on HSM vs cloud KMS — ops estimates 2–4 weeks if customer can provide credentials and compliance docs; add 20% engineering buffer.

If team agrees, I'll send this version to Medisys legal with a short cover note and request clarification on which data they consider "export-controlled."

Thanks,
Olga

Olga Petrov

Thanks for the quick turn. A few clarifying points from our side:
- When we said "controller" in our redline we meant controller for derivative analytics we run on top of customer-provided data (not for raw patient records). We can scope the controller ask to "analytics outputs" if that helps.
- Regarding export-controlled data: our procurement team flagged sample datasets that include cross-border anonymized research cohorts that some of our export counsel think could be covered under EU export rules.
